chunks: And with this chain, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shaybah al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
A bad servant is one who is a humazah lumazah; he faces [people] with one face and turns his back with another.

key_terms.لُمَزَهٌ: One who points fingers or slanders
key_terms.هُمَزَهٌ: One who backbites or whispers evil
key_terms.یُدْبِرُ بِآخَرَ: He turns his back with another [face]

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be a humazah lumazah in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq elaborates on the Quranic terms 'humazah' (slanderer) and 'lumazah' (scorer of faults), characterizing a flawed servant who exhibits hypocrisy by presenting a pleasant countenance while concealing malice. It serves as a practical guide for identifying moral corruption in social interactions, emphasizing the disconnect between outward appearance and inner intent.
